title: Parcel lockers in the lobby
ask: Approve the plan for the lobby parcel lockers, and say whether a resident may name a neighbour to collect for them.
note: Five units across three repos. Every rule in the model holds in this plan, and the run before review shows the two it broke.

product.problem: Couriers leave parcels at the front desk, which closes at eight. Residents who work late wait a day for their parcel, and the desk runs out of room on busy weeks. The new lobby lockers sit unused because nothing tells a resident which door holds their parcel.

users.need: Hears the moment a parcel lands, and opens its locker with a code at any hour.
Takes over parcels nobody collects, and hands each one only to the resident it is for.
Picks a free door on the locker screen and closes it on the parcel.

goals: A resident knows within a minute that a parcel is waiting, and which door holds it.
No parcel stays in a locker past its deadline.

nonGoals.what: Returning a parcel to the courier
nonGoals.why: Couriers already collect returns from the desk.

requirements.title: Know when a parcel lands
requirements.text: When a courier closes a locker on a parcel, the resident gets a message with a pickup code within a minute and sees the parcel in the app. The code opens that door only.

requirements.title: Nothing sits in a locker for good
requirements.text: A resident has two days to collect and can ask once for one more day. After that the front desk takes the parcel out and keeps it for the resident.

rollout.says: Residents of the east wing get codes for the bank by the east lifts.
Every resident gets codes, and couriers stop leaving parcels at the desk.

risks.title: A power cut keeps every door shut
risks.bound: The doors stay locked and the parcels stay safe. The sweep does not run while the bank is down, so no parcel moves to the desk by mistake.

risks.title: Text messages cost money per send
risks.bound: Push is the default. Only residents who chose texts get one, one per parcel.

defaults.says: The two days count from the moment the courier closes the door.
defaults.note: Counting from the next morning would give late drops more time.

items.title: How does a late parcel reach the front desk?
items.why: A parcel past its deadline must not hold a door.

options.label: An hourly sweep puts it on the desk list
options.detail: The desk empties the listed doors on its rounds.

options.label: The door unlocks itself at the deadline
options.detail: The parcel sits behind an open door until the desk comes.

items.title: How a door moves
items.why: Every rule holds in this plan.

says.WellTyped: Every value stays in its allowed set
says.OneParcelPerDoor: A door never holds two parcels
says.ExtraDayOnlyOnce: A parcel gets one more day at most once
says.NothingPastItsWindow: No parcel stays in a locker past its deadline
says.NoDeadlock: The door can always move on

terms.means: the six digits that open one door, sent to the resident when the parcel lands.
two days after the drop, or three with the extra day.

runs.label: This plan
runs.note: The bridge refuses a busy door, and a parcel gets one extra day at most.

runs.label: Before review
runs.note: The bridge took a parcel for any door, and the app let a resident ask for days without limit.

before:OneParcelPerDoor.text: Before review, a courier could close a busy door on a second parcel, and the first resident's code opened both. Now the bridge answers Door in use and the courier picks another door.

before:ExtraDayOnlyOnce.text: Before review, a resident could ask for one more day again and again, and the door stayed busy.

chosen: One extra day, then the front desk
The resident who needs longer collects from the desk, which keeps parcels for two weeks.
other: Fewer trips to the desk, and a busy door for most of a week.
